correctness.rationale: The original Finding uses the unqualified condition λ²=−1 for row three and says it gives a disjoint partition in every characteristic. Over F₂ with λ=1 this condition holds, but row three would give C₄=384 whereas the algebra is commutative and C₄=0. The intended proof already excludes λ=1 before splitting by 1+λ². The complete corrected RESULT.md under /workspace/repairs/2/ makes the stratum order four, fixes the overbroad rank-increment sentence at A=B=C=0, and states the actual checker scope. Re-audit: the PBW product has coefficient λ^(jk) on x^(i+k)y^(j+l), and 1 and x²y² commute with everything. For λ≠1 set h=1+λ, k=1+λ². For h≠0 and a nonzero linear part the four output rows are independent: if v≠0 use x² and xy for the two middle rows, otherwise use xy and y²; the highest-degree row has a pivot on x²y or xy², and the first row is nonzero on x or y. This gives q⁷(q²−1) elements. With zero linear part the lower-degree block has rank 0,1,2 for respectively 1,q²−1,q³−q² quadratic triples because h²AC=B² has q² solutions. If k≠0 the last row extends every nonzero rank-one block and every rank-two block except A=C=0,B≠0. At the zero block it is freely specified by D,E. If k=0 it extends each rank-one block in q²−q of the q² last-row choices, and never extends a rank-two block. These counts, times the free q², recover all coefficients including the exceptional fourth-root row. When h=0 and λ≠1 the resulting 3-by-3 block has zero determinant and its two-by-two minors include signed squares of u,v,B, giving rank two exactly off the central locus. In characteristic two k=0 forces λ=1, handled only by the commutative case. Rank-nullity gives q^(9−r) commuting partners and the stated probability. Proof checked algebraically; the finite-field transcript is supplemental and was not used as an all-field proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact centralizer dimension census of a standard low-dimensional noncommutative family over all finite fields, not just a pointwise experiment. The order-four condition changes the support of the adjoint rank distribution while leaving the center and maximal rank unchanged, so neither datum nor the known fixed-cube specialization detects the transition. The counts also give commuting-pair probabilities and expose exactly where the rank jump fails. No claim about conjugacy classification or centralizer algebra types is needed.
